analysis:
Examined both threat-model excerpts, file metadata, the submodule pointer update, and the MediaIngest patch against the canonical definition index and supplied details. MediaIngest.swift head lines 773–776 and 798 expand the exact, case-insensitive inline-video header allowlist with video/mov and video/x-m4v; non-data URLs remain outside that allowlist, and the visible path still calls dataFromDataURI with maxMediaDecodedBytes. docs/threat-model.yaml lines 1969–1972 aligns T-050 with those aliases while retaining the MP4/QuickTime container, resource-cap and external-reference restrictions. No concrete regression is established by these changes: aliases alone need not introduce a new container parser, disk artifact, authorization path or billing behavior. The remaining attestation, cache, fan-helper and reward prose is unchanged according to the complete documentation range map, not newly implemented or independently revalidated here.
Material coverage limit: libs/mlx-swift-lm line 1 changes the pinned dependency, but its implementation diff is absent. Integration must examine that revision's changes, especially MemoryBackedVideoAsset and MLXVLM/MediaProcessing interactions with MediaIngest: actual MP4/QuickTime byte validation, forbidAll reference restrictions, bounded resource-loader ranges, cancellation, memory ownership, and preservation of decoded-byte/duration/pixel/aggregate limits. These contracts matter to A-001, T-050, TB-007 and availability; dependency changes may also affect T-010, T-028 and T-041. The documentation and new comment are not proof of the dependency's controls. Further review is needed to resolve this PR-specific dependency uncertainty; no vulnerability is inferred from missing source.
